summary: Anthropic launched Claude Science, a beta AI workbench app that integrates research tools, databases, and computing resources for scientists into a multi-agent Claude environment.

mechanisms.reason: The product is built around a coordinating agent that spins up specialist sub-agents and reviewer agents to execute multi-step scientific work, shifting the unit of work from a human using tools to agents executing delegated tasks.
mechanisms.quote: Users interact with a generalist coordinating agent with access to over 60 curated skills and connectors pre-configured for genomics, single-cell, proteomics, structural biology, cheminformatics, and more. These agents can spin up others and engage with specialist agents created by users.

mechanisms.reason: Multi-agent decomposition with sub-agents, specialist agents, and reviewer agents per task implies many more model calls per research task than a single-agent interaction.
mechanisms.quote: These agents can spin up others and engage with specialist agents created by users.

mechanisms.reason: The described architecture holds large datasets and context in memory across a running session rather than reloading, increasing per-session context/memory footprint.
mechanisms.quote: Because its agents work inside a running session that holds context in memory, even massive datasets only need to be loaded once.

practices.reason: The actor-critic multi-agent pattern (a content-generating agent paired with a separate reviewer agent for accuracy and citation checking) is a concrete orchestration technique with a stated outcome that a team could adapt for similarly document-heavy pipelines.
practices.quote: A key component of the workflow, enabled by Claude Science, is the use of actor-critic pairs: one agent creates content while a separate reviewer agent evaluates it for accuracy and citation fidelity.

practices.reason: A reviewer agent that automatically flags incorrect citations, untraceable numbers, and figure-code mismatches is a transferable self-checking/monitoring method for validating AI-generated analytical outputs.
practices.quote: a reviewer agent inspects the outputs, flagging incorrect citations, untraceable numbers, and figures that don’t match their underlying code, and self-correcting as it goes

practices.reason: The product connects to existing lab infrastructure (SSH, HPC login nodes, Modal accounts) and third-party skill toolkits like NVIDIA BioNeMo, which is an integration surface worth noting but not a required or forced change for most teams.
practices.quote: It runs on your lab’s own infrastructure—your laptop, Linux box, or HPC login node—so large or sensitive datasets never have to leave the systems they’re already on
